licence_rule: CC0 or CC-BY only; no NC/ND/editorial

categories.title: 1 · Work (jobs and companies)
categories.concept: A stone waystation / milestone pillar with inscriptions

candidates.name: Boundary way road marker stone
candidates.author: matousekfoto
candidates.recommend_reason: The only milestone scanned in a forest: the moss, leaf litter and scale already match Act III.
candidates.note: A tall mossy road marker and a smaller companion stone, scanned on a forest floor with leaf litter. Already looks like it belongs on our path. The face is mostly blank, so the inscriptions would be our own decal.

candidates.name: Richmond Milestone
candidates.author: artfletch
candidates.note: Georgian milestone with crisp carved lettering ('VIII MILES FROM HYDE PARK CORNER'). The best real inscription here, but the text is London-specific and the stone is clean and urban.

candidates.name: Mijlpaal uit de Renaissance
candidates.author: The National Museum of Antiquities
candidates.note: Renaissance milestone column with a carved Latin inscription. CC0 (no credit needed). It's a museum piece, so there's no moss. 1M faces, so it needs simplifying.

candidates.name: Sandstone Pillar
candidates.author: megalitharchive
candidates.note: Weathered sandstone waymarker pillar with ivy, scanned where it stands. Very natural, but there's no readable inscription.

categories.title: 2 · Games
categories.concept: A ring of standing stones / a game board carved in a stump / a stone chess table

candidates.name: Callanish
candidates.author: megalitharchive
candidates.recommend_reason: The most dramatic, photographic standing-stone ring under 1.5M faces. The stones can be lifted off the base and set in a clearing.
candidates.note: The Callanish standing stones (Isle of Lewis): tall and lichen-covered, on a grass base. 438k faces for the whole ring. It's a well-known real site. The licence is fine, but some visitors may read it as 'that place in Scotland'.

candidates.name: Chessboard made of concrete
candidates.author: Goromor
candidates.note: A weathered concrete park chess table with the chequerboard set into its top. Small (36k faces). Reads as 'game' instantly; less ancient, more found.

candidates.name: Stone Table & Benches
candidates.author: Eydeet
candidates.note: Mossy slab table with two benches on a turf base. Quiet and natural. We would add the game board ourselves.

candidates.name: Chess Set
candidates.author: Riley Queen
candidates.note: Alternative idea: Poly Haven's CC0 chess set, left mid-game on Poly Haven's 'Tree Stump 01' (from the same pine forest collection as our trees). Two CC0 assets combined, and the stump matches the forest exactly.

categories.title: 3 · Landing pages built for people
categories.concept: A cluster of old hanging lanterns

candidates.name: Lantern 01
candidates.author: Rajil Jose Macatangay
candidates.recommend_reason: CC0, photoreal, light enough to repeat into a cluster, and the glass gives us real warm light sources in the forest.
candidates.note: Classic brass hurricane lantern with a hanging handle. CC0, 34k faces. Repeated 5 to 9 times at different heights from a branch, it becomes the cluster.

candidates.name: Wooden Lantern 01
candidates.author: James Ray Cock
candidates.note: Wooden candle lantern with a carry handle. CC0, 8k faces. Rustic. Mixed in with Lantern 01, it adds variety to the cluster.

candidates.name: Old oil lamp
candidates.author: rudavin
candidates.note: Worn green hurricane lantern with dents and rust. 479k faces, which is heavy for an object we repeat; it would need simplifying.

candidates.name: Arabian Hanging Lamps
candidates.author: cha
candidates.note: Five brass hanging lamps, already grouped. 13k faces. The coloured glass reads Middle-Eastern rather than old forest, but it could be re-tinted.

categories.title: 4 · Stories and experiences
categories.concept: A ruined stone archway with light through it

candidates.name: Gunnersbury Park Arch
candidates.author: artfletch
candidates.recommend_reason: A real freestanding ruined arch, already overgrown, with a tall pointed opening for shafts of light.
candidates.note: A freestanding ruined Gothic arch (a park folly) on its own base, with ivy and moss on crumbling stone. 660k faces. Exactly the brief: a pointed opening that light can pour through.

candidates.name: Old Stone Gate
candidates.author: magann
candidates.note: Rough stone wall with a rounded gateway and moss at the base. 158k faces. Wider and lower; it reads as an old estate gate.

candidates.name: Garden Arch Photogrammetry
candidates.author: bent_bacherach
candidates.note: Overgrown brick-and-stone Gothic garden folly with carved stone windows. 299k faces. Lush, but the brick makes it more garden than forest.

candidates.name: Počitelj Fortress - Stone Arch (Scaniverse)
candidates.author: JFN
candidates.note: Rough rubble-stone arch fragment from Počitelj fortress. 157k faces. Very real texture, but the scan has ragged edges we'd need to hide in foliage.

categories.title: 5 · Art and writing
categories.concept: An abandoned easel, or an old writing desk

candidates.name: Crank easel
candidates.author: Virtual Museums of Małopolska
candidates.recommend_reason: A light museum scan of a real antique easel, and the most direct object for 'art'.
candidates.note: An old crank-adjusted studio easel, scanned by a Polish museum. 53k faces. Clean, real wood. Left among the pines with a blank or weathered canvas, it becomes 'abandoned'.

candidates.name: Wooden Easel | dirty and painted
candidates.author: lil_bentley
candidates.note: Wooden easel with paint drips and wear. 23k faces. Modelled, not scanned, but convincing and already looks used.

candidates.name: Underwood Typewriter Vintage Free Raw Scan
candidates.author: Jordan F
candidates.note: An extra idea for the writing half: an antique Underwood typewriter (raw scan), left on a stump or a rock. 89k faces. Dark, worn metal; very photographic.

candidates.name: Writing Desk
candidates.author: Osian CG
candidates.note: Small antique writing desk with a chair, books and an inkwell. 57k faces. Fits 'writing', but furniture standing in a forest needs more around it to look like it was left there.

categories.title: 6 · Tools and engineering
categories.concept: An old forge/anvil, or an orrery/astrolabe

candidates.name: Anvil 1
candidates.author: Beer Knight
candidates.recommend_reason: A real outdoor scan, already on a stump: the tool object that looks most like it was found in the forest.
candidates.note: A weathered anvil on a mossy tree stump, scanned outdoors. 292k faces. It's already sitting on wood and earth, so it drops straight into the forest.

candidates.name: Old Anvil
candidates.author: pomiary.inzynierskie
candidates.note: Rusty anvil on a wooden block. 200k faces. A cleaner studio-style scan; a solid backup.

candidates.name: Armillary sphere (1771)
candidates.author: Virtual Museums of Małopolska
candidates.note: Armillary sphere from 1771 (Jagiellonian University collection): brass rings on a turned base, with a compass. 309k faces. Beautiful and very 'engineering', but a delicate indoor object.

candidates.name: Astrolabe
candidates.author: Virtual Museums of Małopolska
candidates.note: 14th-century astrolabe. CC0, 515k faces. It's a small hand-held object, so it would need a plinth or stump to stand on.

categories.title: 7 · Earlier selves (hidden easter egg)
categories.concept: An old standing mirror, or a small stone well / reflecting basin

candidates.name: Old Water well - Dinan
candidates.author: noxfcna
candidates.recommend_reason: A real overgrown scan that suits the forest. Still water gives the 'see yourself' idea without a man-made mirror.
candidates.note: Round fieldstone well with ferns growing out of it, on a grass base (Dinan, Brittany). 388k faces. Add a dark water surface inside and it becomes the reflecting basin.

candidates.name: Mirror
candidates.author: eucocker
candidates.note: Antique cheval (tilting, free-standing) mirror with clouded, dirty glass. 120k faces. Modelled, not scanned, but strong, and uncanny standing alone between trees.

candidates.name: Venice well 3D Scan Asset
candidates.author: Marcin.Adamski1
candidates.note: Venetian octagonal stone well-head with a lid, on a slab base. 41k faces. Lighter and cleaner than the Dinan well; more formal.

candidates.name: Ornate Mirror 01
candidates.author: James Ray Cock
candidates.note: Gilded arched mirror. CC0, 14k faces. It's a wall mirror, so it would lean against a trunk or rock: a softer, stranger version of the standing mirror.
